text: Ships on the bay. Morning in Maima. Down on the bay, something strange is coming. You are a child of Maima, a Taino village above Saint Ann's Bay. You and your family are fictional. The ships, the canoes and the red moon were real.

key: Bread for bells. The strangers stay on their ships. They are hungry, and they want to trade.
text: Bread for bells. The strangers stay on their ships. They are hungry, and they want to trade.

key: The paddlers. Two big canoes are ready. Cousin is going with them.

key: The ten canoes. Half a year has gone by. Nobody has come back across the sea.
text: The ten canoes. Half a year has gone by. Nobody has come back across the sea.

key: The red moon. The strangers' leader has sent for the leaders of the villages.
text: The red moon. The strangers' leader has sent for the leaders of the villages.

key: When the ships left. A year has passed since the ships came. Now a new ship is in the bay.

key: Back in 2026. The same hill, more than five hundred years later.
text: Back in twenty twenty-six. The same hill, more than five hundred years later.

key: Xaymaca. For a year, the people of Maima fed the strangers on those ships. The written accounts we have come from the Spanish. Here in Jamaica, part of the story is still with us. Every time we eat bammy, we taste something the Taíno passed down.
text: Xaymaca. For a year, the people of Maima fed the strangers on those ships. The written accounts we have come from the Spanish. Here in Jamaica, part of the story is still with us. Every time we eat bammy, we taste something the Taíno passed down.

key: Grandmother lifts the cloth. The zemi looks back at you.

key: It is carved from very hard, dark wood.

key: Its eyes and teeth are made of shell.

key: The Taino believed a zemi held a spirit.

key: Grandmother keeps it safe while the strangers are here.

key: You flip the flat cake with a stick. It smells good.

key: Now the cake bakes on the hot clay griddle.

key: The sailors gave it for the big basket of bread.

key: But where are the paddlers?
